clue.text: Jenny takes drink from champion of 15

definitions.note: 15 is the answer to 15-across, the cue game, whose great champion was the Australian Walter Lindrum

parts.note: Jenny Lind was the famous Swedish soprano of the nineteenth century
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A woman called Jenny accepts a drink from a sporting champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' is not any girl but the singer Jenny Lind. Walter Lindrum, an Australian, dominated professional billiards in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Lindrum held the world professional title in the cue game, so he is a champion of it.

clue.text: Politicians are backward in amending bills

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the reworked letters of the other word
amending a text changes it, so the letters of the word bills are rearranged
backward tells us to read the word are from right to left

explanation.surface: Politicians are said to be reactionary when it comes to changing legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are backward' reads as politicians being reactionary, but 'backward' only turns the little word 'are'. 'amending' reworks BILLS, and 'in' puts the turned word into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberals are members of a political party, so they are politicians.

clue.text: It's about mother breaking record in Paris

definitions.note: the clue points to the famous cathedral found in Paris, so the definition is a place rather than a noun phrase

indicators.note: breaking into a word means splitting it open to sit inside

parts.note: to note something is to record it; a note is also a written record
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
dam is the word for the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother sets a new record while in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the great cathedral of Paris, and 'It's ... in Paris' points to it. 'breaking' puts the two short pieces inside the record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gothic cathedral on the Ile de la Cite is the best-known building in the French capital.

clue.text: Begin again-employer upset 'me

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a user is one who employs something, so an employer

explanation.surface: Someone asks to start again because their boss has upset them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the employee's mood, but in a down clue it turns the employer word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to start once more after a pause.

clue.text: Suitable course for speakers ?

definitions.note: meet is an old word meaning fitting or proper

indicators.note: for speakers says the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: the meat is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone asks which training course would suit public speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: MEET in the sense of fitting survives in 'it is meet and right'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means fitting or proper, as in the prayer-book phrase about what is right.

clue.text: Stuff to put away in Cornwall

definitions.note: the clue points to a place found in Cornwall, so the definition is a location

parts.note: to pad is to stuff or fill out
to stow is to put away or pack

explanation.surface: Someone packs and stores things on a holiday in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England; PADSTOW is a fishing port on its north coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Padstow is a harbour town on the north Cornish coast.

clue.text: Table-ware in the shop window

definitions.note: the clue points to what a shop window is made of, so the definition names a material by where it is found

parts.note: a plate is an item of table-ware
a glass is another item of table-ware

explanation.surface: Crockery and glasses are on display in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: plate and glass are each table-ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Large shop windows are glazed with thick flat sheets of polished glass of this kind.

clue.text: Might make Celt read a book of laws

definitions.note: the decretals are a collection of papal decrees forming part of canon law

indicators.note: the letters of the words Celt read might be made into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A Celt might be made to read a legal code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might make' reworks CELT READ into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decretal is a papal decree, and the Decretals are a compiled volume of canon law.

clue.text: Time for scoring

parts.note: the speed of a piece of music, set down when a composer writes a score, rather than a moment to score a goal

explanation.definitionFit: The pace at which music is played is its time, marked on the score.

clue.text: Poet gets direction to go abroad

parts.note: W is west, a compass direction
aller is the French verb meaning to go, so it is what 'to go' is abroad

explanation.surface: A poet is told to travel overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' asks for a foreign word: French 'aller' means 'to go'. Edmund Waller was a seventeenth-century English poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Waller wrote 'Go, lovely rose' and other lyrics in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Is David's wife a city blue-stocking?

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
a blue-stocking is a learned woman, a she with a BA degree

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether King David's wife was an educated city woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue-stocking is an educated woman: SHE + BA, a Bachelor of Arts. Bath is an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Bathsheba was married to King David after the death of Uriah.

clue.text: Arabian ship ?

parts.note: not a vessel at sea but the beast called the ship of the desert, carrying loads across Arabia

explanation.definitionFit: The animal is nicknamed the ship of the desert, and the one-humped kind is the Arabian.

clue.text: Man enters borders of French city

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: rims are borders or edges
he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man crosses the frontier of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' signals the container. RHEIMS is the old English spelling of Reims, in Champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims is the cathedral city in Champagne where French kings were crowned.

clue.text: Writer appears to run away from girl

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: An author seems to flee from a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the tool, PEN, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a woman's first name, famous as the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: City crank chopped trees

parts.note: a winch is turned by a crank handle, and the words are used for one another

indicators.note: trees that are chopped are cut up, so the letters of the word are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric in town cuts down trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' looks like an eccentric but is a handle, WINCH; 'chopped' reworks TREES into ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is the cathedral city in Hampshire, once the capital of England.

clue.text: Bookmaker has a bit on the Oaks?

definitions.meaning: a page, one of the sheets that make up a book
a part growing on oak trees, the foliage

explanation.surface: A bookie places a small bet on the Oaks horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is an English flat race at Epsom, so 'Bookmaker' and 'a bit' read as betting. In fact leaves make a book and grow on oaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A page of a book and a blade of foliage on a tree are both called by this word.

clue.text: Break for a game ? On the contrary !

definitions.text: Break for a game ? On the contrary !

parts.words: Break for a game ? On the contrary !
parts.note: reversed, the clue asks for a game for a break: the cue game in which a run of scoring shots is called a break

explanation.definitionFit: In this cue game a break is a sequence of scoring strokes, so it is the game for a break.

clue.text: How paratroopers made casual visits ?

definitions.meaning: parachute troops arrive by being let fall from aircraft

explanation.surface: Paratroopers pay friendly informal calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroops are released from planes, and the phrasal verb also means called round unannounced.

clue.text: A criterion for flying?

definitions.meaning: a flag that is flown, especially a royal or regimental banner

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a benchmark of flying skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard, and a banner flown is one too.

clue.text: Sham claim ?

definitions.meaning: an assertion of right, as a pretender's to a throne

explanation.definitionFit: A pose is pretence, and the older sense is a claim, as a pretender makes to a throne.

clue.text: Confined to the East of France without company for 'the festival

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: est is the French word for east

explanation.surface: Someone stays alone in eastern France for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the French east goes round the company. French 'est' means east.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Number in favour of speaking ?

indicators.note: speaking says the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: for means in favour of, as opposed to against

explanation.surface: Some figure supports public speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' says FOR is heard, giving the number spelt FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit after three is a number.

clue.text: Some point in a four-shilling rate

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for a shilling, so four shillings are four S letters
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A point at issue in a rate of four shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: S stands for a shilling, the old British coin worth a twentieth of a pound, so four shillings is SSSS. 'in' puts E after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to evaluate its worth, as a valuer does.

clue.text: Ask for coppers-about to call up

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: d stood for a penny, a copper coin, so coppers are two of them

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to name someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Someone demands money and phones the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' look like police but are pennies: D was the old British penny. 'up' turns the call word, and 'about' puts the two Ds around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand is to request something firmly.

clue.text: A dashing fellow

parts.note: not a stylish man but one who runs short races at top speed

explanation.definitionFit: A runner of short races dashes, rather than being elegant.

clue.text: Lift the beams, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be spoken and heard

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hoist the roof timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like timber but means rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it.

clue.text: Tyrant is clean, as it were ?

definitions.meaning: to take the spots off something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dictator is free of blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as DE-SPOT, to remove spots.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler is a despot, and to de-spot is to remove marks.

clue.text: Some lover and his lass

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A line from the song about a lover and his lass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes Shakespeare's song 'It was a lover and his lass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's name, so she can be any young man's girl.

clue.text: Girl is put in charge, in time

indicators.note: put, with the closing in time, says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A woman is put in charge in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the phrase 'in charge'; 'put ... in' then places that abbreviation inside the period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Mr. Harding's air-raid shelter, perhaps ?

definitions.meaning: Mr Harding is the title character of Trollope's novel about a hospital's keeper
the one in charge of a shelter, as an air-raid warden was

explanation.surface: Mr Harding's bomb shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Septimus Harding is the hero of Trollope's novel 'The Warden'. In wartime Britain, air-raid wardens supervised shelters and the blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel is named for Mr Harding's post, and a wartime shelter had a warden in charge.

clue.text: Slight for one advancing a bob?

parts.note: bob is slang for a shilling, abbreviated s
a lender advances money

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a small loan of a shilling is too little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bob' is British slang for a shilling, written s. 'advancing' means lending money, not moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and slender both mean thin or small.

clue.text: Dan comes in before the music

definitions.note: the clue means a slow movement, a piece of music

indicators.note: comes in says one piece enters the other

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dan arrives ahead of the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' signals the container; 'before' is the Latin word, not a position marker.
explanation.definitionFit: An andante is a movement played at a moderate walking pace.
